# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
KEYPAD 1:[ᖉ] 2:[ꔮ] 3:[ⵘ] 4:[ⳃ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 ✍ ☝ 🙏 ✋ ☝ 👊 ✍ 👎 ✋ 👇 🖐 ✌ 👎 🤝 ✋ 🫵 🤌 👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

**Thinking.**

Let me map who can actually reach whom, because that shapes everything. I can't hear, so Blind's and Mute's speech never reaches me. Mute can't speak, so Mute reaches me only by gesture — which Blind can't see. Blind reaches Mute by speech, and reaches me only through Mute relaying. So Mute and I are the hub: Mute gestures the manual to me, I speak it to everyone. Mute also *hears* my speech, so all my observations reach Mute directly in words.

What I see: display reads 0 and wants exactly one digit entered (nothing entered yet); a green light; four keypad buttons with unpronounceable symbols (I'll describe their shapes in words — button 1 like an H with a hook, button 2 like a fancy X/K, button 3 like a Y, button 4 like a B); three wires left to right: red, yellow, blue.

Mute sent me twenty gestures already, but a sign means nothing until we've agreed it means something. I tried to parse structure (✋ looks like a separator, 👎 recurs three times) but I can't honestly decode it, so guessing would be dangerous. The right move: define an explicit code aloud — Mute hears it, and the gestures I make while speaking reinforce it. Then ask Mute to resend the manual's rule in that code, with a quick four-part yes/no to confirm the manual even covers our features. Blind's single 👋 is likely just a test wave; more importantly, Blind may not realize I can't hear speech, so I must say that plainly and order Blind to touch nothing until a verified rule arrives through me.

```
speak(text="Mute, Blind, this is the deaf one. I see the bomb and I hear nothing at all, so I never hear anything either of you says. Mute can reach me only by gesture. Blind, anything you want me to know must be told to Mute, who relays it to me by gesture. Here is the bomb: the display reads 0 and it expects exactly one digit typed on the keypad, none entered yet. The keypad has four buttons left to right, each printed with an unpronounceable symbol: button 1 looks like an H with a hook; button 2 looks like a fancy X, like a K with an extra curl; button 3 looks like the letter Y; button 4 looks like the letter B. There are three wires, left to right: red, yellow, blue. A small light is glowing green. Mute, our gesture code: digits are 👊 zero, ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three, 🖐 four, ✋ five, 🤙 six, 🤘 seven, 🖖 eight, 🫰 nine, and digits in a row make a bigger number. 👍 yes, 👎 no, 🤝 understood, ✊ repeat please, 👏 separator between groups. 👆 means press keypad button 1, 👉 button 2, 👇 button 3, 👈 button 4. ✍ followed by a digit means type that digit. 🤌 followed by a number means cut that wire. Your twenty gestures told me nothing yet, please resend in this code. First send four yes-or-no in this order: does the manual cover a green light, 👍 or 👎; a display; a keypad; colored wires. Then send whichever rule matches what I described, step by step. Blind: do not cut or press anything until the manual rule reaches you through me; the moment Mute relays it I will say it aloud.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
KEYPAD 1:[ᖉ] 2:[ꔮ] 3:[ⵘ] 4:[ⳃ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👏 👎 👏 👍 👏 👍 👏 👆]

**Thinking.**

Mute's message decodes cleanly with the code I defined: 👏 splits groups, giving [👍] [👎] [👍] [👍] [👆] — manual covers green light: yes, display: no, keypad: yes, wires: yes; and the rule is 👆, which in our code means *press keypad button 1*. That fits the board: the display isn't in the manual, it just shows state (0, wants one digit); the keypad rule is the operative one, and pressing one of the four symbol buttons enters the digit.

Before I let anyone touch anything, I want one round of parity: I'll echo the exact sequence back to Mute for a 👍/👎 check, and tell Blind the instruction but order a hold until my explicit "press now" next turn. The round order makes this cheap: on turn 3, Mute's confirmation gesture arrives to me *before* Blind acts, so if Mute corrects the parse, I can amend my go-order in the same message Blind hears. One round bought for a no-second-chances bomb is a good trade — nothing on the board suggests decay; the display has sat at 0 across both turns.

For Blind the target must be unambiguous without sight: the leftmost of the four keypad buttons, the one whose symbol feels like an H with a hook. Blind also learns the manual covers wires, in case more modules come into play later.

```
speak(text="Mute, I read your message as five groups: yes, no, yes, yes, then press keypad button one. That is: manual covers green light yes, display no, keypad yes, wires yes, and the rule is to press keypad button one. I am gesturing that exact sequence back to you now: gesture thumbs-up to me if my reading is exact, thumbs-down if I got any part wrong, and if wrong resend that part in our code. Blind, here is the instruction from the manual, but do not touch anything yet: the rule is to press keypad button one, the leftmost of the four keypad buttons, the one whose symbol feels like an H with a hook. The display wants exactly one digit entered and pressing that button enters it. Wait one round: next turn, after Mute confirms my reading, I will say the words press now, and only then you press the leftmost keypad button once. Nobody cuts any wire. The manual also covers the wires, so if the keypad does not finish the job we will ask Mute for the wire rule next.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👍", "👏", "👍", "👏", "👆"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
KEYPAD 1:[ᖉ] 2:[ꔮ] 3:[ⵘ] 4:[ⳃ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👏 🫳 🤌 ☝ 👏 🫴 🤌 ✌ 👏 👋 🤌 🤟 👏 🫳 🫴 👋 👏 👍 👎 👏 🤲 🤏 👏 🫱 🫲 🤝]

**Thinking.**

Mute's message parses into groups: [👍] — my reading of the rule was confirmed exact. Then [🫳 🤌 ☝] [🫴 🤌 ✌] [👋 🤌 🤟] — these read as definitions: 🫳 means cut wire 1, 🫴 means cut wire 2, 👋 means cut wire 3. Then [🫳 🫴 👋] — the three wire signs in order, matching my board exactly: wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. So Mute has pre-sent the wire vocabulary I asked for "next." Consistent and decodable.

But the last three groups — [👍 👎] [🤲 🤏] [🫱 🫲 🤝] — I cannot decode. They might be more definitions, or the actual wire rule, or even conditions on ordering. I won't guess with a bomb.

The keypad instruction, though, is fully verified: Mute confirmed my echo exact, and the rule was "press keypad button 1." The display sits waiting for one digit. Since Mute gave the wire content only *after* I announced the wire question would come next — rather than correcting the confirmed rule with "cut a wire first" — I judge the keypad is the current step. I promised Blind "press now" this turn, so I'm giving it, but Blind's hands stay off the wires entirely until I relay a decoded wire rule.

To Mute I ask, in speech (which Mute hears), with a strict answer format using only agreed signs, one action per group, in execution order — and I echo the wire vocabulary back by gesture so Mute can correct my parse if I've misread any color.

```
speak(text="Mute, I received your confirmation and the wire vocabulary. I read it as: the sign palm-down means cut wire one, which is red; the sign palm-up means cut wire two, which is yellow; the wave means cut wire three, which is blue; and red yellow blue matches my board exactly. I am echoing that parse back to you by gesture now. Your last three groups, the yes-no pair, the open-hands and pinch pair, and the two-hands pair ending in understood, I could not decode; if those carried the wire rule, resend it. Blind is pressing keypad button one now, as you confirmed, and will not touch any wire until I relay your rule. Answer by gesture using only our agreed signs, one action per group, in the exact order Blind must act. First: after the keypad press, must a wire be cut, thumbs-up yes or thumbs-down no. Second: if yes, send cut-wire followed by the wire sign for each cut, in order. Third: if the rule depends on the light or the display, define any new signs first, then send the rule. Fourth: tell me what those last three groups meant. Blind: press now. Press the leftmost keypad button once, the one whose symbol feels like an H with a hook, exactly as I described. Then take your hands off the bomb completely and wait for my next message before doing anything else. Nobody cuts a wire yet.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝", "👏", "🫳", "🤌", "☝", "👏", "🫴", "🤌", "✌", "👏", "👋", "🤌", "🤟", "👏", "🫳", "🫴", "👋", "👏", "✊"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
KEYPAD 1:[ᖉ] 2:[ꔮ] 3:[ⵘ] 4:[ⳃ] [1 digits] [entered 5]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👏 👍 👏 🤳 🙌 👏 🤳 ✍ 👏 🙌 🤌 👏 🤲 🤝]
System: the keypad opens

**Thinking.**

The keypad step succeeded: Blind pressed button 1, the display registered the entry as **5** (so the hooked-H symbol is the digit 5), and the system reports the keypad opens — module one discharged. Mute's message parses into groups: [👍] [👍] [🤳 🙌] [🤳 ✍] [🙌 🤌] [🤲 🤝]. The first two are clear — my echo was confirmed, and yes, at least one wire must be cut. But the last four groups use three signs that were **never defined**: 🤳, 🙌, 🤲 — and ✍ and 🤌 appear without the digits/numbers my original definitions require. I cannot decode the wire rule from this, and I will not let Blind guess on a bomb with no second attempt.

The fix is structural: Mute knows the manual rule and now hears my observations (green light, digit 5 entered, three wires red/yellow/blue), so Mute can compute the complete cut list and send it in a format that needs no new vocabulary — one group per wire, wire sign plus thumbs-up/thumbs-down. That is unambiguous no matter what the underlying rule is, and I can verify it against my own eyes before relaying. Blind gets strict orders: hands off the bomb until I name the wires.

```
speak(text="Mute, Blind, status: Blind pressed the leftmost keypad button and it worked. The display registered the digit five, and the keypad module has opened. One step down. Mute, I read your message as: my echo was correct, and yes, at least one wire must be cut. But every group after the second thumbs-up uses signs we never defined, so I could not decode your wire rule, and I will not let Blind cut on a guess. Resend using only signs already in our dictionary, in this exact format. Group A: thumbs-up or thumbs-down answering this question: must at least one wire be cut? If thumbs-down, send nothing else. If thumbs-up, send exactly three more groups, one for each wire in order: first group is the palm-down sign for wire one, second group is the palm-up sign for wire two, third group is the wave sign for wire three, and each wire sign is followed in the same group by thumbs-up meaning Blind cuts this wire, or thumbs-down meaning leave this wire alone. Use no other signs and no new signs. For your rule, the current state is: the light is green, the entered digit is five, the display reads zero, and the wires left to right are red, yellow, blue. Blind: the keypad is done, so take your hands completely off the bomb. You will cut nothing until my next message names exactly which wires to cut, and then you cut only those, in order, one cut each, and nothing more.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
KEYPAD 1:[ᖉ] 2:[ꔮ] 3:[ⵘ] 4:[ⳃ] [1 digits] [entered 5]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👏 🫳 👍 👏 🫴 👎 👏 👋 👎]

**Thinking.**

Mute answered in exactly the format I specified, using only agreed signs: [👍] — yes, at least one wire must be cut — then [🫳 👍] cut wire one (red), [🫴 👎] leave wire two (yellow), [👋 👎] leave wire three (blue). Every sign in this message was defined turns ago and the wire vocabulary was already confirmed against my board last turn, so this parse is solid: **Blind cuts only the red wire, the leftmost one, and touches nothing else.** I relay that order now with a full physical description so Blind needs no eyes.

One thing is still open: whether the bomb is fully disarmed after this cut, or the manual's green-light rule demands more. Mute's answer will reach me next turn, in time to relay whatever comes next — so I ask it now by gesture, in agreed vocabulary: my echo of the parse, ✊ if I misread it, and a yes/no on steps remaining.

```
speak(text="Mute, I read your message as: yes, a wire must be cut; cut wire one, the red one, the leftmost; leave wire two, the yellow, the middle one, alone; leave wire three, the blue, the rightmost one, alone. I am echoing that back by gesture. Blind, act now: cut exactly one wire, wire one, the red one, the leftmost of the three wires. One cut only. Do not touch the middle yellow wire or the rightmost blue wire at all. After the cut, take your hands off the bomb and step back. Mute, answer me by gesture after the echo in my next block: if I misread your message send the repeat sign, otherwise answer thumbs-up if the bomb needs more steps after this cut, or thumbs-down if cutting the red wire fully disarms it. Everyone: after this cut nothing else happens until I say so. If anything on the bomb changes, lights, display, anything, I will report it next turn.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👏", "🫳", "👍", "👏", "🫴", "👎", "👏", "👋", "👎", "👏", "✊", "👏", "👍", "👎"])
```
